# Qupath

## addQuPathPolygons

Add QuPath annotations to a SIRUP object as polygons.

`addQuPathPolygons` reads a GeoJSON file that QuPath exported. It converts the annotations to the coordinates of a spatial sample in a SIRUP object. It adds a buffer to each polygon, so that every spot whose circle touches the polygon becomes a member of it. Then it stores the polygons in the object.

```r
addQuPathPolygons(
  x,
  path,
  sample_id = NULL,
  class = NULL,
  keep_unclassified = TRUE,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  image = NULL,
  buffer = NULL,
  replace = FALSE,
  include_boundary = TRUE,
  validate = TRUE
)
```

Arguments:

- `x`: A SIRUP object.
- `path`: Path to the QuPath GeoJSON file.
- `sample_id`: Name of the spatial sample that the annotations belong to. A SIRUP object with one spatial sample does not need it. A multi-sample object does.
- `class`: Class names to keep. If `NULL`, the function keeps all classes.
- `keep_unclassified`: Keep annotations that have no class (default `TRUE`)? The function ignores this if you set `class`.
- `image_scale`: Image scale of the polygon coordinates, for example `"hires"`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in `x`. If `x` has no value, you must give one, and the function stores it in `x`. A value that differs from the stored one gives an error.
- `swap_coords`: Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in `x`. The rules are the same as for `image_scale`.
- `image`: Name of the Seurat image to use. If `NULL`, the function uses the only image of the sample.
- `buffer`: Distance to grow each polygon, in the coordinates of the object. If `NULL` (default), the function uses the spot radius. Use `0` for no buffer.
- `replace`: Replace the stored polygons of this sample (default `FALSE`)? If `FALSE`, the function adds the new polygons to the stored ones, and the polygon IDs must not repeat.
- `include_boundary`: Count spots on a polygon edge as members of the polygon?
- `validate`: Validate the updated object?

Value: The updated SIRUP object. Spatial metadata and receptor records get the new `polygon_id` values.

## readQuPathPolygons

Read QuPath annotations as SIRUP polygons.

`readQuPathPolygons` reads a GeoJSON file exported from QuPath. It returns a polygon table. Pass the table to [`addPolygons()`](sirup-polygons.md).

```r
readQuPathPolygons(
  path,
  sample_id = NULL,
  class = NULL,
  keep_unclassified = TRUE,
  scale = 1
)
```

Arguments:

- `path`: Path to the GeoJSON file.
- `sample_id`: Sample name to add to all polygons. A multi-sample SIRUP object needs it. Use `NULL` for a single-sample object.
- `class`: Class names to keep, for example `"GC"`. If `NULL`, the function keeps all classes.
- `keep_unclassified`: Keep annotations that have no class (default `TRUE`)? The function ignores this if you set `class`.
- `scale`: Number that multiplies all x and y values. See Details.

Value: A tibble with the columns `polygon_id`, `class`, `vertices`, and `sample` (only if you set `sample_id`). `vertices` is a list-column of tables with the columns `x` and `y`.
